section_summary: The section concludes a set of U.S. comments on Japanese banking reform and contains successive drafts debating how technical advice should be offered under occupation policy. Later correspondence concerns the Industrial Bank of Japan’s efforts to attract American investment and U.S. securities registration requirements. The final despatches and enclosures address Japanese duties on tobacco and liquor and tax exemptions for goods sold for foreign exchange.

subfiles.title: Comments on proposed Japanese banking reform
subfiles.about: Detailed comments assess credit institutions, securities holdings, lending limits, bank capital, supervision, and penalties.
subfiles.summary: The concluding pages urge stronger Bank of Japan control over credit and recommend changes to proposed rules on government credit corporations, postal savings, stock disposal, loans, bank capital, charters, and examinations. The authors regard many remaining proposals as consistent with sound banking practice and offer further consultation.

subfiles.title: Draft observations on central bank and private banking reform
subfiles.about: Draft passages favor interim expansion of Bank of Japan powers while questioning immediate comprehensive reform.
subfiles.summary: These draft passages argue that economic conditions and unresolved questions about a separate banking board make immediate, sweeping monetary reform premature. They propose interim changes to the Bank of Japan law, including reserve and supervisory powers, and discuss loan limits, capital ratios, and banks weakened by inflation.

subfiles.title: Draft Part I of telegram on Japanese banking reform
subfiles.about: Draft instructions limit SCAP’s role and frame technical comments as informal views rather than U.S. policy.
subfiles.summary: The draft advises SCAP to leave detailed reform to Japanese authorities and share technical comments only after a high-level request.

subfiles.title: SCAP telegram C 64251 on proposed bank laws
subfiles.to: Department of the Army, Washington, D.C.
subfiles.about: SCAP reports Japanese progress on revised bank laws and requests final U.S. views by November 1.
subfiles.summary: Japanese proposals broadly match principles discussed with SCAP, and submission to the Diet is expected around mid-November.

subfiles.title: Reference slip forwarding another banking cable redraft
subfiles.about: McDiarmid forwards a revised Part I after discussion with Barnett.
subfiles.summary: McDiarmid says the redraft better states his office’s position and may satisfy the Army.

subfiles.title: Proposed Part I of telegram to SCAP
subfiles.about: The draft defines the scope of SCAP advice on Japanese banking reform.
subfiles.summary: It recommends general, high-level guidance while allowing technical comments in response to Japanese requests. Those comments are to be identified as informal agency views, not U.S. or SCAP policy.

subfiles.title: Alternative wording on solicited technical advice
subfiles.about: A proposed paragraph conditions technical advice on a Japanese request.
subfiles.summary: It says solicited comments may aid recovery but must be described as informal technical views.

subfiles.title: Draft Part I on voluntary Japanese banking reform
subfiles.about: The draft balances Japanese initiative, requested advice, and possible general instructions from SCAP.
subfiles.summary: SCAP should avoid pressing detailed legislation, but may give general instructions if lack of reform threatens recovery and U.S. aid. Technical comments would remain informal.

subfiles.title: Part I draft citing SCAP message C-65458
subfiles.about: A revised draft permits technical consultations after a high-level Japanese request.
subfiles.summary: It describes Japanese responsibility for banking legislation and limits U.S. comments to informal technical advice.

subfiles.title: Further copy of Part I draft on banking reform
subfiles.about: A second near-identical draft addresses technical assistance for Japanese banking legislation.
subfiles.summary: It repeats that Japanese authorities should develop legislation and that U.S. technical comments are informal.

subfiles.title: Revised Part I with alternative wording
subfiles.about: Marked draft language revises when SCAP may intervene and share technical comments.
subfiles.summary: The draft favors voluntary Japanese reform, general instructions if necessary, and technical comments in response to solicited advice. Its changes emphasize that agency comments do not express U.S. or SCAP policy.

subfiles.title: Revised Part I on Japanese banking reform
subfiles.about: Another marked draft sets limits on SCAP instructions and transmission of technical material.
subfiles.summary: It proposes general instructions to Japanese leaders where needed and informal transmission of technical comments following a request.

subfiles.title: Memorandum proposing new Part I for banking reform telegram
subfiles.about: Bishop proposes replacement language to align the banking telegram with NSC 13/2.
subfiles.summary: The proposed insertion would reduce detailed SCAP involvement, route requests for expert advice to Washington, and leave specific reform measures to Japanese authorities. The memorandum quotes occupation policy provisions supporting this change.

subfiles.title: Alternative paragraph on expert technical information
subfiles.about: A draft paragraph proposes how Washington studies could be furnished to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Detailed studies could be sent to Washington and later supplied to Japan for information and discretionary use.

subfiles.title: SEC letter forwarding Industrial Bank of Japan correspondence
subfiles.about: The SEC alerts State to possible securities registration issues in the bank’s investment materials.
subfiles.summary: Louchheim encloses the bank’s letter and the SEC reply concerning possible U.S. circulation of investment materials.

subfiles.title: Industrial Bank of Japan letter on foreign capital
subfiles.about: The bank offers information and intermediary services to support renewed American investment in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Kishi sends a history of the bank’s foreign borrowing and a proposed investment program. He describes its reorganization, credit investigation capacity, and willingness to help prospective investors in Japanese firms.

subfiles.title: SEC reply on Securities Act registration
subfiles.about: The SEC chairman explains registration requirements potentially applicable to the bank’s U.S. solicitation.
subfiles.summary: Hanrahan says circulation of the proposed investment program may constitute an offer to sell securities under the Securities Act of 1933. He outlines registration requirements and requests details of the bank’s U.S. activities before offering further advice.

subfiles.title: State Department letter to Army on Japanese investment outreach
subfiles.about: State asks Army and SCAP to share U.S. securities guidance with Japanese financial institutions.
subfiles.summary: Knapp forwards the SEC exchange and urges guidance that would help Japanese institutions avoid damaging investor confidence.

subfiles.title: Knapp letter to Louchheim
subfiles.about: Knapp sends Louchheim a copy of his letter to the Army.
subfiles.summary: The brief letter encloses Knapp’s response to West about the bank’s investment outreach.

subfiles.title: Army reply on forwarding SEC guidance to SCAP
subfiles.about: The Army confirms that the correspondence was sent to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Porter says SCAP was asked to share Hanrahan’s guidance with appropriate business and financial institutions.

subfiles.title: Supplementary report on Japanese tobacco import duty
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch reports discussion of the 355 percent duty on tobacco imported for non-Occupation use.
subfiles.summary: ESS suggested applying the duty to cigarettes alone and lowering rates for cigars and cut tobacco.

subfiles.title: Applicability of Japanese Customs and Internal Taxes to Non-Occupation Imports and Taxation of Invisible Exports
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch explains tobacco and liquor tax policy and exemptions for export bazaar sales.
subfiles.summary: Japanese authorities began collecting the 355 percent tobacco duty on July 15, while taxes on liquor imports remained suspended pending customs reform. The despatch also describes expanding sales of Japanese goods for foreign exchange and summarizes four enclosed memoranda on duties and export bazaar tax exemptions.

subfiles.title: Applicability of Customs and Internal Taxes to Non-Occupation Imports
subfiles.about: ESS accepts tobacco duties but advises postponing liquor taxes and broader tariff enforcement.
subfiles.summary: Marquat supports tobacco duties from July 15 while recommending customs law revision before broader enforcement.

subfiles.title: Imposition of Custom Duty and Domestic Excise Upon the Imports
subfiles.about: The Finance Ministry proposes collection procedures for liquor taxes and tobacco duties on non-Occupation imports.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum sets out bonded storage, reporting, and collection procedures for imported liquor and tobacco. It distinguishes goods destined for Occupation forces from those delivered to other foreign nationals.

subfiles.title: Taxation of Invisible Exports
subfiles.about: ESS accepts temporary tax exemption for qualifying Japanese goods sold for foreign exchange.
subfiles.summary: Exemption requires foreign exchange payment, benefit to Japan’s economy, and purchase for personal use.

subfiles.title: Imposition of Domestic Excise and Transaction Tax at Export Bazaars
subfiles.about: The Finance Ministry asks whether export bazaar sales may temporarily avoid domestic taxes.
subfiles.summary: Hirata proposes exemption if sales use non-yen currency and resale is prevented.
